diagram_name: Where in Paul's Life Was Each Letter Written?
chapter_title: Paul at Ephesus, Part 1: The Apostle's Life, Letters, and Ephesian Years
learning_objective: The learner will organize the seven undisputed letters onto a timeline of Paul's life, using one clue from inside each letter, placing all seven in an accepted period within two attempts.
specification:
Type: timeline **sim-id:** paul-letters-on-his-timeline
**Library:** vis-timeline
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** organize
**Learning Objective:** The learner will organize the seven undisputed letters onto a timeline of Paul's life, using one clue from inside each letter, placing all seven in an accepted period within two attempts. **Prerequisites:** the seven undisputed letters, Paul's missionary journeys, the Book of Acts, Timothy and Titus, Phoebe and Cenchreae, and the Ephesian imprisonment theory (all defined in the chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner drags each of seven letter cards onto one of six life periods on the timeline and presses Check. A placement is correct when the period is in the "Accepted periods" column in Content. Mastery is all seven placed in accepted periods within two Checks. Reading the clues and the event infoboxes is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Paul's letters were written in the order they appear in the New Testament, so Romans came first. (2) All the prison letters were written in Rome at the end of his life. (3) Paul wrote letters throughout his thirty years of travel; in fact the seven come from about ten years, most of them from the third journey. **Instructional Rationale:** Organizing evidence into a structure is an Analyze task: the learner must read each clue, connect it to a place and a period in Paul's life, and fit the seven into one chronology. Accepting more than one period for the prison letters teaches that some placements are debated, while the clue-based feedback shows why the rest are firm. **Content:** Life periods shown as bands on the timeline (dates approximate, labeled "c."): | Band | Period | Dates | What happened | |---|---|---|---| | A | Call and early years | c. 33–46 CE | Call near Damascus; Arabia; first visit to Jerusalem; Syria and Cilicia | | B | First journey | c. 46–48 CE | Cyprus and southern Anatolia | | C | Second journey | c. 49–52 CE | Macedonia, Athens, eighteen months in Corinth | | D | Third journey | c. 52–57 CE | Two to three years in Ephesus, then Macedonia and Corinth | | E | Prison in Caesarea | c. 57–59 CE | Arrest in Jerusalem; two years held in Caesarea | | F | Voyage and Rome | c. 59–62 CE | Shipwreck on Malta; two years of house arrest in Rome | Point events shown on the timeline, each with an infobox: - c. 49 CE: Meeting in Jerusalem about Gentile believers and the law (Chapter 11). - 51–52 CE: Gallio proconsul of Achaia, dated by an inscription found at Delphi. - c. 52–55 CE: Paul in Ephesus. - c. 62–67 CE: Paul's death in Rome, according to later tradition (labeled "tradition"). Letter cards, in this fixed order, each showing the letter's name and its clue: | # | Letter | Clue shown on the card | Accepted periods | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 1 Thessalonians | Paul stayed behind in Athens and sent Timothy to Thessalonica; Timothy has just come back with good news. (1 Thessalonians 3:1–6) | C | Acts has Timothy rejoin Paul in Corinth after Athens, on the second journey, about 50 CE. It is the earliest surviving letter. | | 2 | Galatians | Paul tells of the Jerusalem meeting about circumcision and of a later quarrel with Peter at Antioch. (Galatians 2) | D or C | It must be later than the Jerusalem meeting of about 49 CE; most scholars place it in the third journey, about 54–55, and some in the second. | | 3 | 1 Corinthians | "I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost." (1 Corinthians 16:8) | D | Paul is in Ephesus, on the third journey, about 54 CE. | | 4 | 2 Corinthians | Paul has gone on into Macedonia and found Titus there with news from Corinth. (2 Corinthians 7:5–7) | D | After leaving Ephesus, Paul traveled through Macedonia on the third journey, about 55–56 CE. | | 5 | Romans | Paul is about to take the collection to Jerusalem and commends Phoebe of Cenchreae, Corinth's port. (Romans 15:25–26; 16:1) | D | Written from Corinth at the end of the third journey, about 56–57 CE, just before the trip to Jerusalem. | | 6 | Philippians | Paul writes in chains and sends greetings from "the praetorium" and "Caesar's household." (Philippians 1:13; 4:22) | D, E, or F | A prison letter. Scholars place it in an Ephesian imprisonment (third journey), in Caesarea, or in Rome; the guard and household could exist in any provincial capital or in Rome. | | 7 | Philemon | Paul, "an old man and now also a prisoner," sends Onesimus home to Colossae and asks Philemon to prepare a guest room. (Philemon 9, 22) | D or F | A prison letter. Ephesus, near Colossae, fits the plan to visit soon; Rome is the traditional view. | **Provenance:** Periods, dates, clues, and accepted periods come from the chapter sections "Paul's Missionary Journeys," "Timothy and Titus," "The Seven Undisputed Letters," "The Letter to the Galatians," "First Corinthians," "The Letter to the Romans," and "Phoebe," and from the verses cited. Dates are approximate reconstructions; the sim labels them "c." and shows the note "Dates are scholars' reconstructions and differ by a year or two." **Rules:** - A card may be dropped only on a band (A–F), not on a point event. - A placement is correct when its band is in the card's "Accepted periods"; for cards with more than one accepted period, every listed period counts as correct. - Check evaluates all seven cards at once; it is available only when all seven are placed. - After the first Check, correct cards lock in place; incorrect cards return to the tray for a second attempt. - After the second Check, any card still incorrect moves to its first-listed accepted period and is marked "shown." **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads the six bands and four point events on the timeline. 2. The learner reads each letter card's clue and drags the card onto a band. 3. The learner presses Check. 4. Correct cards lock and show their "Why" text; incorrect cards return with a hint. 5. The learner places the returned cards and checks again. 6. The learner should notice that four of the seven letters land firmly in band D, the third journey, around Paul's time in Ephesus, that the two prison letters may belong there too, and that only the prison letters remain debated. **Feedback:** Seven cards, placed in any order, two Checks. On each correct card: "Accepted. [Why]" On each incorrect card after the first Check: "Not this period. Look again at the clue: who is where, and what has just happened?" After the second Check: "[n] of 7 placed in accepted periods," with the "Why" text shown for every card, and any card still wrong marked "shown." Mastery message when all seven are accepted within two Checks: "All seven placed. At least four of them come from the years around Ephesus." **Starting State:** The timeline from 30 to 70 CE with the six bands and four point events; the seven cards in a tray in the fixed order; the question "Where in Paul's life was each letter written?" **Chapter Anchors:** Seven undisputed letters; 1 Thessalonians about 50 CE from Corinth, the earliest; 1 Corinthians from Ephesus about 54 CE; Romans from Corinth about 56–57 CE; at least four of the seven, perhaps six, from the five years around Ephesus; Philippians and Philemon written from prison, place debated (Ephesus or Rome); Gallio 51–52 CE; Paul in Ephesus about 52–55 CE.
